text:
A: Hello! There she is. Donna, is it? Can you hear me alright?
B: Yeah. Hiya.
A: I'm Darren. Last one for me, this. Where are you, then?
B: Plumstead. South-east London.
A: Oh, right, London. I'm Basingstoke. Did you have to come far for this, or is it all on the laptop?
B: Sorry, what was that?
A: Ha, no, ignore me, obviously it's on the laptop. That was a stupid question. Anyway, yeah. What do you do?
B: Nothing at the minute. I was cleaning offices in Woolwich, early mornings. Contract ended.
A: Ah, that's a pain. Looking for something?
B: Sort of. Cleaning or kitchen porter. Something early so I'm back for my daughter.
A: Makes sense. I manage a builders' merchants, yard and trade counter, fourteen staff. Funnily enough the woman I just spoke to used to do accounts at one. Small world today. The bloke before that's a Saints fan from Basingstoke and all, so it's been like a reunion.
B: Right.
A: How many kids have you got, then?
B: Two. Kyle's sixteen, Mia's eleven.
A: Sixteen, so GCSEs?
B: Yeah. This year.
A: My Ellie's the same. Mocks in a couple of weeks. She's alright, to be fair, she's more organised than me. Doesn't take much, mind. How's your lad getting on?
B: Erm, he's clever enough, he just doesn't do anything. PlayStation till all hours. He wants to do electrics after, so I keep telling him, you need maths for that, you need English. He thinks I'm nagging. I am nagging, but someone's got to, do you know what I mean? I left school with four GCSEs and I don't want him doing the same.
A: Electrician, that's a good shout, though. Proper trade. I tell you what, the sparks that come in my place, they're not short of a few quid. Half of them drive nicer vans than my car, and I've got an Audi.
B: Yeah, well. He's got to get on the course first.
A: He will. Sixteen-year-old lads are all the same. My son was a nightmare at that age, and now he's at uni in Nottingham, so.
B: Is he?
A: Yeah. Comes home with his washing. Do you drive at all?
B: No.
A: No? How do you get about, then?
B: Walk, mostly. The buses are rubbish. The 53's always late.
A: I'd be lost without the car, me. I sat on the M3 forty minutes on Tuesday, mind, so maybe you've got the right idea.
B: I'm not paying for a car anyway. The electric's gone up enough.
A: Oh, it's criminal, the bills. Anyway, yeah. What do you do on a Friday? Takeaway sort of person?
B: Chinese, if there's money.
A: Curry for us. Every Friday, without fail. The dog sits there looking at you like he's never been fed.
B: You've got a dog, haven't you? I saw it on your picture.
A: Murphy. Black Lab. Ate a tea towel last week. Whole thing.
B: Ha. Mia would love a dog. Not allowed in the flat, though.
A: Probably for the best. Two hundred quid at the vet, that tea towel. More than the—
